transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. It's probably nothing major, but... I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I work in a warehouse, and... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but if a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm sounds, or even if someone is just moving a pallet nearby, it completely pulls me off my count. 

And then I end up... well, I'll realize I've put the wrong numbers into the inventory. I really try to do a good job and be a reliable worker, so making silly mistakes like that is just... it's really not like me. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking for.
Have you had this kind of distractibility since you were a child?

Oh, no, no, definitely not since I was a child. I was always a very good student, very focused. I wouldn't want you to think I've always been... scatterbrained or anything like that. 

Actually, it's really just been recently. Maybe for about a month or so? It's silly, really, but... well, my husband recently stopped working outside the home, and it just kind of threw our whole routine out the window, you know? I'm sure it's just an adjustment period and I'm probably making a bigger deal out of it than I should be. Does that sound like a normal reaction to a change in routine like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you feel this started because of your husband stopping work and the change in your routine?

Well, um... I guess I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. It just seemed like the only really big change that happened recently, so my mind kind of naturally jumped to that. But I really wouldn't want to say for sure that's what caused it. 

I definitely don't want to sound like I'm blaming him, or like I'm just making excuses for my mistakes at work, you know? I really don't know exactly why it started. I'm sorry, I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer for you. Am I being helpful at all, or should I try to think of something else that might have triggered it?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Oh, no, definitely not. I haven't been feeling down or depressed at all. Actually, I've been feeling pretty good! I mean, other than the little silly mistakes at work, of course. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around moping or anything like that. I've always been a pretty positive person, I think. I try to look on the bright side of things, even when there's an adjustment, like with my husband being home more. 

So, no, no depression here. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm glad I'm not depressed, but I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing. Is it okay that I'm just feeling... normal, mood-wise?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean... well, everybody has little everyday things they think about, right? Like just making sure the bills are paid or doing things safely at work—I move freight for a living, so you always have to pay attention to what you're doing. But I definitely don't sit around agonizing over things. 

I really try to just take life one day at a time. I wouldn't want you to think I don't care about my responsibilities, though! I do, very much. I just... I try not to let myself get all worked up over nothing. Is that... does that sound like a healthy way to handle things? I hope I'm answering these right for you, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you been feeling unusually nervous or on edge lately?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I haven't been feeling on edge or nervous at all, really. I mean, I guess anyone can have a little momentary startle if someone drops a heavy pallet at work or something loud happens, but... no, nothing unusual. 

I try to stay pretty calm and collected. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm high-strung or, you know, unable to handle things. I just go about my day as steadily as I can. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being clear enough for you, I just want to make sure I'm answering everything the right way.
Since your husband stopped working outside the home, has that change been causing you stress?

Oh, no, not really. I mean... well, of course, any big change takes a little getting used to, right? But I definitely wouldn't say it's causing me stress. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm complaining about him or that we're bickering at home, because we aren't at all. We get along just fine! It's actually kind of nice having him around more, and I really try to be as supportive of him as I can. I just take it in stride and focus on my own work at the warehouse. 

I hope that's a normal way to react? To just kind of roll with the punches when things change at home? I just want to make sure I'm handling it the right way... and that I'm giving you the right information, of course.
Do everyday sounds seem unusually hard to filter out for you lately?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, warehouses are just noisy places anyway, right? There's always a beeper going off, or a forklift alarm, or someone dropping a pallet. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm bad at my job, because I really try to be so careful, but... lately, those little sounds just kind of pull my attention away. Like, I'll be right in the middle of counting freight, and a noise happens, and my mind just sort of jumps over to it. And then... well, I have to admit, I've accidentally put the wrong numbers into the inventory a couple of times because I lost my place. 

That's actually kind of why I thought I should come in. I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing like I usually do. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I mean, everybody gets distracted sometimes, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by bringing it up to you.
Have you become unusually sensitive to everyday noises lately?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm sensitive to them. It's really just the distraction part I was talking about before. The noises themselves don't bother me or hurt my ears or anything like that. 

I'm not, you know, irritable or snapping at people when things get loud. I really try to be easygoing about it all. It's just that my focus kind of slips away when I hear something. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm explaining the difference right, so I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how I'm acting at work.
Have you been feeling detached from yourself, like you’re watching yourself from the outside?

Oh, goodness, no. I haven't felt anything like that at all. I'm very much... well, I'm just me, right here in my own body. 

I hope you don't think I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that! I promise I'm completely present. I just have that little bit of trouble keeping my focus at the warehouse, like I mentioned, but I definitely don't feel like I'm watching myself from the outside or anything scary like that. 

Is that... is that a common thing to happen to people? I just want to make sure I'm answering all your questions the right way and giving you what you need, but no, I haven't noticed anything like that at all.
Have you recently experienced or witnessed something traumatic at work?

Oh, no, nothing like that. The warehouse is pretty safe, really. We have a lot of safety protocols, and I always try to follow them to the letter. 

I haven't seen any accidents or anything upsetting... it's just a normal job, moving freight around. I hope I didn't give the impression that my workplace is dangerous or that I'm, you know, easily upset by things there. I'm just having that little bit of trouble concentrating, that's all. I'm doing my best to be a good employee, I promise. Did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do unwanted thoughts keep interrupting your attention when you're trying to concentrate?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't really have unwanted thoughts popping up or anything. My mind is usually pretty clear, I think. 

It's really just the noise around the warehouse that pulls my attention away, like I was saying before. I definitely don't have any strange or upsetting thoughts getting in the way. I hope I'm explaining that right... I just want to be sure you know I'm trying really hard to stay focused on my work. I'm not letting my mind wander off into bad places or anything. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
Have you been sleeping poorly lately?

Oh, no, my sleep has been just fine, actually. I always make sure to get to bed at a reasonable hour so I'm rested for my shift. I know how important a good night's rest is, especially with a physical job, so I really try to stay on a strict schedule. 

I'm not tossing and turning or waking up a lot in the middle of the night, if that's what you're worried about. I hope that's a good sign! I really am trying to take good care of myself and do all the right things to stay healthy. Was that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
Do you ever find yourself zoning out or daydreaming so much that you lose track of what you’re doing?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I zone out or daydream like that. I try really hard to stay present and focused on what I'm doing, especially at work. I know it's important to be alert when you're moving things around. 

Sometimes I might just, you know, get a little distracted by a loud noise or someone dropping a pallet, but I don't lose track of time or forget what I'm doing. I always snap right back to it. I'm a very reliable worker, I really am. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound like I'm irresponsible or anything. I take my job very seriously.
Have you been worried that something might be physically wrong with you because of this trouble concentrating?

Oh, goodness, no. I haven't been worrying about anything like that. I'm actually very healthy for my age, I think! I keep up with my regular checkups and try to take really good care of my body, especially since my job keeps me on my feet so much. 

The distraction thing is really just... well, just the normal warehouse noise getting to me a little bit, like I mentioned before. I definitely don't think there's anything physically wrong with my brain or anything scary like that. I hope that's okay to say? I just really don't want to come across like someone who complains about every little thing or overreacts, you know? I promise I'm doing my absolute best to stay strong and keep working hard. Is that the kind of information you needed?
Has this trouble concentrating been seriously affecting how well you function at work?

Well, I wouldn't say *seriously* affecting... I mean, I really try my hardest to do a good job. But, um, I guess there have been a few little mix-ups lately. Just minor things! I've had to double-check with my supervisor a couple of times because of some silly inventory errors I made. It's so embarrassing, but I always make sure to fix it right away so it doesn't cause any real trouble. I just want to make sure they know I'm still dependable. 

And, well, I guess things at home have been a little tense, too. My husband just retired, and we should be enjoying it, but we've been bickering more than usual. It almost feels like we're just tiptoeing around each other instead of settling into this new phase of life. But I'm sure it's just a normal adjustment period, right? I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I'm trying to handle it all as best I can. Does that make sense?
Do you feel your trouble concentrating is mainly because of the tension and adjustment at home since your husband retired?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I really don't want to blame my husband or his retirement for my little slip-ups at work. That wouldn't be fair to him. The tension isn't *that* bad, honestly, we're just... figuring out our new routine together. 

I don't think it's the main reason I've been a little scattered. I probably just need to try a little harder to bear down and focus on my tasks, you know? I hope it's okay to say that. I really don't want to make it sound like my marriage is in trouble or anything, because it's definitely not! We're perfectly fine. I'm just trying to be completely honest with you so I can get back on track. Is that helpful?
Did your trouble concentrating begin after your husband retired?

Well, yes, I suppose the timing does line up that way. It's been going on for about a month now, which is right around the time he stopped working outside the house. 

But I really want to be clear that I don't think it's his fault! It's just... well, our whole usual routine completely changed, you know? After all those years of having a set schedule, suddenly everything is different, and I'm just taking a little while to catch up and adjust to the new normal. I'm sure anyone would feel a little off-balance with a big change like that, don't you think? I just hope I don't sound like I'm complaining about having him home, because I'm really not. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. Does that answer your question okay?
